candidate_source: Mahan 1989 J. Appl. Phys. 65:1578 and Sofo & Mahan 1994 Appl. Phys. Lett. 65:2690 (optimum gap of 6 to 10 kBT); a later range of 6 to 18 kBT is described in recent arXiv work (arXiv 2010.08832, 1901.03999)
note: At kBT = 0.0258 eV (300 K) the 6 to 10 kBT range is 0.155 to 0.259 eV; at 800 K (kBT = 0.0689 eV) it is 0.41 to 0.69 eV, and 6 to 18 kBT is 0.41 to 1.24 eV; the 0.6 cap is 8.7 kBT at 800 K and 23 kBT at 300 K. The literature gives a lower bound on the optimum gap (larger than 6 to 10 kBT), not an upper cap, so the cap is a stated choice. The thesis's second reason (composition-only models extrapolate unreliably to wide-gap insulators) is an empirical claim that this study does not test. Materials Project gaps are PBE and underestimate experimental gaps. Sensitivity row S2 (cap x1.5 = 0.9 eV) is reported.
